To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

negotiations strictly outperform auctions if the buyer has a strong bargaining position, renegotiation is costly for the buyer, and the seller is likely to have superior knowledge of possible design improvements.

negotiations outperform auctions when the buyer is a large, experienced firm that can use its market power in the post-contract phase to extract information from its suppliers, and that negotiations also provide stronger incentives for suppliers to invest in the design of their products.

auctions are less efficient than negotiations because they do not allow for early exchange of information, which is important if sellers are likely have superior information about design improvements and if renegotiation is inefficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of procurement mechanisms for the procurement of complex and customized goods.
the design and analysis of mechanisms to allocate complex goods.
the question of whether auctions are always superior to negotiations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of the procurement mechanism depends on the specific characteristics of the good, the bargaining power of the buyer, the cost of renegotiation and the cost of information.
negotiations are superior to auctions for complex goods.
auctions are not always better than negotiations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
auctions are not necessarily the most efficient mechanism to procure complex goods.
negotiations are superior to auctions if the seller has better information than the buyer about the quality of the good and the renegotiation is costly.
negotiations are superior to auctions in situations where the buyer has the bargaining power and where the seller has the better information about the product design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
negotiations can outperform auctions in the procurement of complex products.
negotiations are a better mechanism for the procurement of complex products than auctions.
auctions are not necessarily the superior procurement mechanism, and that negotiations are often the better choice.
